Title: Global AR Smart Glasses Shipments Grow 148% YoY in H2 2025; Waveguide-based Devices Surge Over 600%
URL: https://counterpointresearch.com/en/insights/Global-AR-Smart-Glasses-Shipments-Grow-148-Percent-YoY-in-H2-2025-Waveguide-based-Devices-Surge-Over-600-Percent
Published: 2026-04-08T00:00:00.000Z
Author: N/A
Highlights:
- In 2025, global AR smart glasses shipments rose 98% YoY, reaching a record high in the market’s history. 
- H2 2025 saw even stronger growth of 148% YoY, fueled by Rokid Glasses scaling up, launch of Meta Ray-Ban Display and new offerings from other OEMs. 
- The video-centric AR smart glasses segment grew over 80% YoY in H2 2025, with leading players RayNeo, XREAL and VITURE capturing a combined 96% market share. 
- The waveguide-based AR smart glasses segment surged over 600% YoY, featuring a more diverse landscape with Rokid, Meta, Even Realities, INMO, Alibaba and Meizu vying for sales and mindshare. 
- We expect global AR smart glasses market growth to continue in the coming years, though recent memory price hikes and geopolitical tensions could pose challenges.
...
In H2 2025, the market recorded a stronger YoY growth of 148%, driven by key industrial developments, including the scale-up in shipments of Rokid Glasses, launch of the Meta Ray-Ban Display, and a range of new products from RayNeo, VITURE, Even Realities, INMO and Alibaba. Amid these favorable market dynamics, both major segments expanded – video-centric AR smart glasses (typically using Birdbath or Flat Prism lenses) grew 80% YoY, while waveguide-based, information-display AR glasses surged by over 600%. As a result, the share of waveguide-based products in the total market increased to 38%, up from only 13% in H2 2024 and 19% in H1 2025.
...
The waveguide-based AR glasses segment exhibited a distinct yet more robust competitive landscape, with companies such as Rokid, Meta, Even Realities, INMO, Alibaba and Meizu vying for market share. Most new products launched in H2 2025 focused on integrating AR and AI with real-life use cases, enabling features such as real-time translation, navigation, speech prompting and, more commonly, camera-based image recognition and encyclopedic Q&A. Since 2025, Chinese OEMs have also begun collaborating with Alibaba to introduce glass-based payment solutions. Among the key OEMs:
...
- Rokid emerged as the leading OEM in shipments in H2 2025, driven by strong initial sales momentum and a successful production ramp-up of Rokid Glasses, which quickly gained traction as an early entrant in the “AR+AI” glasses segment. Production scaled up significantly by the end of June 2025, with Rokid expanding beyond mainland China through telecom operators, eyewear retailers, malls and online channels to broaden regional availability. 
- Meta Ray-Ban Display is the first commercialized smart glasses from Meta with a see-through display. Paired with the Meta Neural Band and deeply integrated with Meta’s mobile ecosystem and Meta AI, the glasses quickly gained popularity among tech enthusiasts. However, supply was constrained in 2025 due to the relatively low production yield of key components. 
- Even Realities ranked third in the segment, capturing a 16% market share with its ultra-lightweight G1 and G2 series glasses, which feature a design resembling traditional prescription glasses. 
- Chinese OEMs INMO and Alibaba followed with 7% and 5% market share, respectively. 
- Alibaba launched the Quark AI Glasses S1 in Q4 2025. The product generated strong market buzz in China due to integration with Qwen AI and Alibaba’s mobile services (Amap, Alipay, Taobao, Feizhu). However, supply constraints and a relatively high price (~$671 official, ~$528 after discounts) limited shipments in 2025. 

 In H2 2025, AR glasses equipped with AI-capable processors, microphones, speakers, cameras and wireless connectivity – classified as “AI glasses” – represented roughly 70% of total waveguide-based AR glasses shipments, up from negligible levels a year earlier. China and the US are currently the largest markets for these devices.
...
We expect the upward growth momentum in the global AR smart glasses market to continue in the coming years, supported by international expansion from leading OEMs, more new entrants, and improving maturity and production yields in key display and optical components. Nevertheless, recent memory price hikes and geopolitical tensions involving the US, Israel and Iran, along with their impact on the global economy, may pose challenges.

In 2025, global production of AI+AR glasses diffraction optical waveguides reached 360,000 units, with an estimated average selling price of $237 per unit. AI+AR glasses diffraction optical waveguides are transparent near-eye display optical components specifically designed for AI+AR glasses. They couple image light output from microdisplays or micro-optical engines into a transparent waveguide sheet via micro-nano diffraction gratings. The light propagates within the waveguide via total internal reflection, and then the image is projected onto the user's eye through the coupling grating, allowing users to see AI captions, real-time translation, navigation prompts, notifications, visual question-and-answer results, icons, or lightweight AR content in a real-world environment. Upstream components include optical glass, resin materials, nanoimprint adhesives, MicroLED/Micro-OLED microdisplays, optical engines, and photolithography/imprinting/inspection equipment; downstream components are AI+AR glasses manufacturers. AR glasses diffraction optical waveguides are transparent near-eye display optical components specifically designed for AR glasses, AI+AR glasses, and smart display glasses. The working principle is as follows: image light output from a microdisplay or micro-optical engine enters a transparent glass or polymer waveguide sheet through a coupling grating. It propagates within the waveguide through total internal reflection, and then the output grating guides the virtual image to the user's eye, allowing the user to see text, icons, subtitles, navigation, translations, AI prompts, or virtual images while viewing the real environment. It is mainly used in consumer-grade AI+AR glasses, industrial-grade AR glasses, and sports/outdoor AR glasses. The head-mounted display application dominates the AR waveguide market, driven by the proliferation of AR glasses, smart helmets, and enterprise headsets. These devices require compact, lightweight, and high-quality waveguides capable of delivering immersive visual experiences.
